characters.name: David Banner/The Hulk
characters.description: As a result, whenever David gets angry or outraged, he transforms into a gigantic, savage green monster. Later on, a lab accident occurred and it took the life of his research partner, Dr. Elaina Marks and the incident was blamed on his alter-ego, with the side effect of causing others to believe that Dr. Banner was killed as well. David is forced to let the world believe he is dead as he travels across the country, looking for a cure for his condition and evading investigative reporter JackMcGee. Actually, I Am Him: Whenever a female scientist of the episode talks about his work, he becomes briefly surprised by how much they're invested in them, and a rare case where he'll openly tell them he's Banner, and they kept his survival a secret. Adaptational Angst Downgrade: David has none of Bruce's more personal issues, such as his relationship with his father Brian, since David and DW's estrangement was the result of the death of his mother, but they reconciled over their differences. It's also the result of Bruce's mental creations of the various Hulks, such as the Gray Hulk/Joe Fixit, The Professor, and more famously, the Devil Hulk, who had been trying to protect him when he was a child. While David does has a level of angst, they were never this deep as comic Bruce's. Adaptational Job Change: In the comics, Bruce was a gamma scientist before turning into the Hulk. In the series, he's an MD and a scientist, and he wasn't exclusively researching gamma radiation. Adaptation Name Change: Sort-of. Bruce is still his middle name, but Banner goes by his first name, which was changed from "Robert" to "David."

characters.name: JackMcGee
characters.description: And Starring: He's billed after Bill Bixby with "Also Starring JACK COLVIN" in the opening credits. He also shares this title with Lou Ferrigno. Anti-Villain: Jack is only after the Hulk because he believes Hulk is responsible for the deaths of David Banner and Elaina Marks. In the "Mystery Man" two-parter however, when he finds out where the Hulk actually comes from, he wants to help the man who becomes the Hulk, unaware that he was talking to David. Beneath Notice: Like David, he has a habit to get into places no authorized personnel should be able to. He was able to infiltrate the Prometheus base just by disguising himself to get in the base. Canon Immigrant: More than four decades after the TV show premiered, ayounger,Gender Flipped, andRace Liftedversion ofMcGeenamed Jacqueline "Jackie"McGeemade her comic debut in 2018'sThe Immortal Hulk. However, she's looking for Banner so she can learn to become like him, not to bring him to justice or help cure him. Cassandra Truth: He's been following Hulk's trail for years, and whenever he brings him up, not many people want to believe him, or chose not to.

characters.name: Laura Banner
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: She was created only for the series; she is partially inspired by Hulk's love interest in the comics, Betty Ross (who eventually married Bruce Banner years after the show ended). The Lost Lenore: David's first one. Her death heavily affects him one year after he failed to save her. It also contributes David's obsession to discover how humans are able to unlock a tremendous amount of strength during their times of need, and find out gamma radiation is the source of it, which leads to him overdosing 2 million units of gamma radiation, and transformation into the Hulk. Posthumous Character: She had been dead for almost a year when the events in the series start, but she does appear in David's nightmares about her tragic demise.

characters.name: Elaina Marks
characters.description: Canon Foreigner: She was created only for the series. Childhood Friends: Implied with David, since she'd had to be David's age before his mother's untimely death. Dying Declaration of Love: As she was dying in the Hulk's arms, Elaina managed to admit to the creature that she had always loved David.Elaina:Oh, God. My poor David. Who will take care of you now? It's okay, it's okay. I don't know if you can understand me, but I want you to know something. Dear David, I have loved you for a very long time. And I always will. (weakly)And I always will... Plot-Triggering Death: Her untimely death is partly the start of David beginning his years-long trek in finding a cure. Secret-Keeper: She was the first to know and experience David's strange condition firsthand, and ended up keeping that secret to the grave.

characters.name: Carolyn Fields
characters.description: All for Nothing: She wanted to use David's cells to regenerate her cells to counter her illness. But alas, a hurricane strikes Hawaii, her illness drives her crazy, David Hulks out, and shedies in the Hulk's and David's arms. Dying Declaration of Love: Only the second one the Hulk ever heard:Dr. Fields:At least we never gave up... trying. (embracing the Hulk with the last of her strength) Oh, I'll miss you, David... Second Love: David had various girlfriends before her, but she becomes his second wife. Secret-Keeper: One ofveryfew people who know that David's alive and of David's secret affliction. Like Elaina, she too ends up keeping that secret to her grave. Your Days Are Numbered: She expected that she has 6 months before her illness takes hold. Her doctor tells her she has two to three weeks to live.

characters.name: Li Sung
characters.description: First appearing in the second season episode, "Another Path", he is a blind Chinese philosopher and martial arts expert who tried to help David control his condition. Back for the Dead: He dies in "The Disciple." Handicapped Badass: He's old and blind, but a very skilled martial artist, easily defeating the villain of his first episode alone, along with many of his mooks. Even the Hulk was just cleaning up after him rather than defusing the threat himself. Secret-Keeper: One of the few who know David's secret; in fact, he figured it out just throughhearinghim transform.

characters.name: DW Banner
characters.description: David's estranged father, a farmer from Treverton, Colorado. Canon Immigrant: The comic version of Banner's father appeared three yearsafterthis version, with adifferent name(Brian), profession (a scientist rather than a farmer) andpersonality. Determinator: He chases after Hulk on a windy morning armed with a rifle, on foot no less, after Hulk unleashes his pent-up childhood anger towards him by lifting a hay wagon. Happily Married: He loved his wife Elizabeth before her tragic death by illness. Her death drove a series of events that led to David becoming a medical doctor instead of a farmer. This is a heavily contrast with Brian, who was an abusive monster to both his wife and child, and ended up killing his wife Rebecca and Bruce ends up cracking his skull on her gravestone in the comics. Only Known by Initials: It'sneverstated what "DW" stands for.

characters.name: Helen Banner
characters.description: David's sister who is a field scientist working on their father's farm. Her fateful reunion with David allows him to figure out how to save the farm. Canon Foreigner: She was created for the TV show; in the comics, Bruce was an only child with his cousinJenniferbeing the closest thing to a sister he ever had. Morality Chain: She tries her best to keep her family together even after their mother passed away. Apparently, David and DW's relationship went south so badly that she had to step in before David decides to leave to be a medical doctor. Secret-Keeper: Not only does she know her brother's condition, but she and her father are among the very few people who know he's actually alive. Small Role, Big Impact: In a meta sense anyway.Word of Godsuggests that there was briefly talk in the studio of having Helen become a female version of the Hulk and get her own show a laThe Bionic Woman, with Marvel overhearing of this and quickly creatingtheir own female Hulk(albeit Banner's cousin rather than sister) in order to retain the rights.

characters.name: Michael Sutton
characters.description: First appearing in the season three episode, "The Snare", he's a deranged millionaire game-hunter who trapped David on his private island. Blood Knight: He's an insane game hunter who loves the thrill of the hunt and killing his "prey",especiallywhen said prey gives him an interesting challenge. Hoist by His Own Petard: He accidentally hits himself withthe tip of one of his poisonous arrows. It led to hisKarmic Death. Hunting the Most Dangerous Game: He had already upgraded to hunting down and killing human beings, but he becomesdelightedwhen he first sees David's transformation:"I saw that beast you turned into David, unbelievable! What was it, how do you do it? It was magnificent, David, magnificent! Make it come back?You hear me, David! Make it come back!"

characters.name: Dell Frye
characters.description: First appearing in the season four two-parter, "The First", he was a bitter old man who once transformed into a creature similar to the Hulk long ago and desired to reclaim that power. Ax-Crazy: Frye was pretty unstable before he met David, when he killed the kid who broke into the Clive house a year previously. His Hulk is very much this when he first transforms, as he tried to kill a doe. The next scene shows that he was deliberately provoking a couple of guys in a bar in order to get back at them, and kills one of them by turning into his Hulk. Canon Immigrant: Much like JackieMcGee, Dell makes his first comic appearance inThe Immortal Hulkas Delbert John Frye, though ismuch youngerand has a case ofAdaptational Heroismalong with sufferinga far more terrifying outcomethan being able to turn into a Hulk-like creature. Comic-Book Movies Don't Use Codenames: Dell's Hulk form is simply named "Frye's Creature" in the credits. Drunk on the Dark Side: Dellrevelsin transforming into a murderous beast who can eliminate all his enemies and isdyingto get that ability back at any cost in the first part.

characters.name: Jasmine
characters.description: Cain and Abel: Jasmine's sister is a terrorist, and the final villain David/Hulk faces. Everyone Has Standards: She's an espionage spy, but she wouldNever Hurt an Innocent. When she infiltrated Ron Pratt's lab, she only knocks out the security woman Betty and that she'll wake up an hour later. When she does goes to Pratt's lab, she tries to drag him to safety when he was knocked unconscious. The Lost Lenore: This time, David doesn't lose her. She loses him.

characters.name: Donald Blake/Thor
characters.description: Adaptational Species Change: Thor is a Norse God in the comics, but here, he's a Viking. Bullying a Dragon: Thor harasses David into becoming the Hulk. Well, he got what he wanted when David transforms, and Hulk resists his attacks. Decomposite Character: Donald Blake and Thor are separate characters here. In the comics, Donald uses Mjollnir to turn into Thor. The Nicknamer: Thor calls the Hulk "Troll". Outside-Context Problem: Thor is the first instance of magical beings existing in the universe of the series involving radiation mutations and gamma monsters. This takes David by surprise since while he has faced supernatural beings and psychics, but not mythological beings.

characters.name: Matt Murdock/Daredevil
characters.description: The Man without Fear himself who becomes David's lawyer after he wasWrongly Accused. He later finds out David transforms into the Hulk after he saves him. Handicapped Badass: He is blind, but his other senses are amplified to help him navigate his surroundings.

characters.name: Wilson Fisk/Kingpin
characters.description: Bald of Evil: Kind of. He's balding, but still has hair. Karma Houdini: He escapes justice from Daredevil and flees. Rogues' Gallery Transplant: Sort of. He's normally a villain forSpider-Man, but also a villain for Daredevil. He's a first for Hulk. The Unfought: Neither David nor Hulk confronts him at any point.

characters.name: Bruce Banner
characters.description: A brilliant scientist who, after exposure to gamma radiation, was tragically cursed to transform into the Incredible Hulk whenever stressed or angered. Now, he is on the run from the military while he tries to find a cure for his condition. Adaptational Nice Guy: Bruce Banner can be neurotic and self-absorbed in the comics, partly from his childhood trauma. In this version, Bruce is much friendlier with only the occasional lapse in judgement. Even in his origin story, he developed a Gamma Reactor to benefit mankind as opposed to building a bomb for military purposes. Adaptational Angst Downgrade: There is no indication this Bruce had an abusive childhood. Cursed with Awesome: Despite the fact that his entire life has been ruined because of his savage alter-ego, the only reason Bruce survives his brushes with death is due to transforming into the Hulk wherever needed. Deadpan Snarker: Bruce can deliver his share of dry lines whenever needed.

characters.name: The Hulk
characters.description: The jolly green giant himself, who Bruce Banner turns into whenever angered. Hulk is childlike and good-natured, but also violent when provoked. Adapted Out: The other Hulks don't show up in this series other than himself and Grey Hulk. Battle in the Center of the Mind: He and Grey Hulk would battle each other to see who'd come out when Bruce was angered. Savage Hulk tends to win more often. At least once, during "Mind Over Anti-Matter", both Hulks team up against a common foe. Because You Were Nice to Me: Hulk usually helps out whenever someone is nice to him, such as saving the pre-Zzzax MitchMcCutcheonfrom the Hulkbusters. But Now I Must Go: He does this to the kid and the Candian Hunters in "Man to Man, Beast to Beast".

characters.name: Grey Hulk
characters.description: Banner's other alter ego, the Grey Hulk emerged as a result of the Nutrient BathGone Horribly Wrongat the end of the first season. After sorting out the mess in "Hulk of a Different Color", Grey Hulk and Savage Hulk wrestle for who gets to be let out. Grey Hulk is far more intelligent than his green counterpart, a rude jerk but not above reason or willingness to help when necessary. Adaptational Heroism: Aside from "Hulk of a Different Color", Grey is a shadyAnti-Heroat worst compared to the absolute villain he could be. Even his "Joe Fixit" stint in the cartoon was a ploy with She Hulk to take down a crime boss, rather than being a job he did for the mafia. Adaptational Name Change: "Joe Fixit" is not his name in this show, as he's only referred to as Grey Hulk. Battle in the Center of the Mind: Grey and Savage Hulk often duke it out inside of Bruce's landscape to see who'd be unleashed whenever he got angry. Grey would occasionally win out. Composite Character: A retroactive example. As was written at the time, Grey Hulk was simply the original Hulk before Savage dominated. It wouldn't be until years later that Devil Hulk was revealed to be the original instead.

characters.name: Betty Ross
characters.description: Bruce's girlfriend and a scientist. Her father, Thunderbolt Ross, is the man in charge of hunting Bruce down. Adaptational Intelligence: In the comics, Betty Ross was simply present on Gamma Base due to her father being in charge. In this series, she's a scientist in her own right. Adaptation Dye-Job: Betty is a brunette in the comics but has blonde hair in this show. It might have been based off of the look Betty had during the Pantheon arc, where she dyed her hair blond with Marlo Chandler's help, though she kept it short unlike the show's ponytail. Everyone Loves Blondes: Betty is blonde in this show due toAdaptation Dye-Joband both Bruce and Talbot are in love with her, though she only has eyes for the former. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: Betty has blonde hair and is a kind, loving woman.

characters.name: Rick Jones
characters.description: A teenager who accompanies and tries to help both Bruce and Hulk out of guilt for accidentally causing Bruce’s accident. The Atoner: Rick was present at the Gamma Reactor site when Samuel Sterns sabotaged it, and if it weren't for Bruce pulling him to safety before it exploded, it would have turned him into the Hulk. Now, he seeks to watch Bruce's back while helping him find a cure for his condition, as repentance. Fusion Dance: At the end of the "Light and Darkness" three-parter, after accidentally being knocked into the nutrient bath where Banner and the Hulk are being re-merged, something goes wrong and Rick ends up being turned into his own version of the Green Hulk. Fortunately, he getsdepoweredby the Leader at the end of the next episode. Totally Radical: It is present in his characterization, though to a subtle extent.

characters.name: She-Hulk
characters.description: Bruce's lawyer cousin. After an encounter with Doctor Doom leaves Jennifer badly injured, Bruce uses his blood to giver her a transfusion. But his gamma-infused blood causes her to mutate into the Sensational She-Hulk. Action Girl: Jen has no issue keeping up with the Hulk in the asskicking department. Adaptational Dumbass: Downplayed. This show places a great deal of focus on Jen's humorous and sexual aspects but put little emphasis on her legal career. The one episode where we do see her practicing law doesn't paint her as being very competent in the field. Amazonian Beauty: Musclebound, and breathtakingly beautiful. This IS She-Hulk, after all. However, the musclebound part gets downplayed in season 2 where she gets a slimmer physique. Boisterous Bruiser: Jen is energetic and jovial, both in and out of battle.

characters.name: Glenn Talbot
characters.description: General Ross’ second-in-command, who secretly loves Betty and wants Bruce out of the way. Everyone Has Standards: When he discovers General Ross wandering the desert and blindly firing shots at imaginary Hulks towards the end of the "Light and Darkness" three-parter, he realizes that he's in no fit state to issue orders and ignores his command to go in pursuit of the Hulk, instead trying to bring Ross back to base for medical care.

characters.name: Gabriel Jones
characters.description: A SHIELD agent on loan to Ross. Hazy–Feel Turn: Gabriel sort of helps Betty in the Season 1 finale and doesn't really interfere again afterwards. In the second season, he and She-Hulk even flirt for a bit, implying aRelationship Upgrade. Teeth-Clenched Teamwork: Gabriel and Ross are often at odds, with Gabriel willing use underhanded tactics to get a one up for SHIELD that comes at the military's expense.

characters.name: The Leader
characters.description: Adaptation Origin Connection: In this cartoon, Samuel Sterns was both the scientist who sabotaged the Gamma Reactor, leading to Bruce Banner's exposure and transformation into the Hulk, and was transformed into the Leader after falling into gamma-irradiated sludge left at the site of the accident. In the comics, Sterns was a janitor who was working at a chemical plant before he randomly was exposed to gamma radiation in a freak accident, and he never had any connection with the Hulk at all. Added Alliterative Appeal: Often gets into this while speaking. Bad Boss: Usually talks down to Gargoyle, although Gargoyle frequentlygives as good as he gets. Because Destiny Says So: Helovesto assert that destiny intends for him to take the Hulk's power and use it to conquer the world, on the basis that his actions leading to both his and Banner's mutations are clearly a sign of his cosmic importance. Big Bad: The main antagonist of the series.

characters.name: Gargoyle
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: He becomes attracted to She-Hulk the moment he sees her, and goes to great lengths to win her over, which she does not appreciate. Adaptational Villainy: A bit. The Gargoyle was a one off villain who very quickly turned against his Soviet masters once Bruce and Rick provide him a cure. Here, while he hasNoble Demonqualities, he's firmly a villain even when not looking for a cure to his condition. Always Someone Better: While he's legitimately smart in his own right, his understanding of gamma radiation pales compared to Bruce Banners, and his general intelligence is below that of the Leader's. This is why he's willing to play second-fiddle to the Leader. Ascended Extra: A one-off villain from the first ever issue ofThe Incredible Hulkbecomes a far more prominent character here. Borrowed Catchphrase: When the Leader is temporarilydepoweredand reverts to Samuel Sterns, Gargoyle twice attempts to steal Sterns' signature catchphrase of "So says the Leader!" by turning it into "So says the Gargoyle!" Played for laughs in that Gargoyle declares it still sounds stupid even when he's doing it, and laments about how hard it is to come up with a snappy signature line.

characters.name: Abomination
characters.description: Adaptational Angst Downgrade: With no mention of his human identity as Blonsky, it can be safely assumed Abomination doesn't carry the same shame over being trapped inside of a monstrous body. Adaptational Dumbass: Much less intelligent than his comics counterpart, down to being nothing more than a snarling beast in his first appearances. Even when he talks, he's not as smart as Blonsky in the comics. Adaptational Wimp: While still strong enough to tangle the Hulk, due to his diminished intelligence he's not much better than a mook compared to the personal menace Abomination can be in the comics. The Dragon: Is the Leader’s primary enforcer and is as powerful as the Hulk. You find yourself wondering why the Leader doesn’t just swap bodies with him. Decomposite Character: Abomination doesn't seem to have ever been Blonsky in this continuity. As such, he's supremely lacking in theTragic Monsteraspects of the character.

characters.name: Ogress
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: Her devotion to the Leader has distinct tones of romantic infatuation, which the Leader finds disgusting due to how ugly she is. Adaptational Backstory Change: In the comics, Ogress was one of the five surviving gamma mutates left after the Leader nuked the town of Middleton with a gamma bomb to create his own gamma mutate enforcers with which to battle the Hulk. Here, she's a genetically engineered lifeform created by the Leader in aUterine Replicatorfrom a sample of the Hulk's DNA, making her technically anOpposite-Sex Clone. Adaptational Dumbass: In the comics, Ogress was a lawyer and a fairly successful one, if frustrated with her role as a defense lawyer. Here, she's just aDumb Musclebrute of the Leader's. Brawn Hilda: Ogress is a woman, but unlike She-Hulk, she's a hideously deformed monster, with an ape-like posture, fur-covered limbs, a missing eye, big bushy eyebrows, an upturned, flattened nose, broad jaw, forward-thrust brow, and missing teeth. Canon Foreigner: Inverted. There reallyisan Ogress in the comics, although she was a relatively obscure Hulk villain, and the cartoon preserves theBroad Strokesof her back-story as a super-powered enforcer created by the Leader.

characters.name: The Gamma Warriors
characters.description: Blade Below the Shoulder: Two of the Gamma Warriors are equipped with cybernetic weapon arms; a female with a chainsaw for a right arm, and a male with a cybernetic right arm that ends in two rotating blades, similar to a helicopter propeller. A third male Gamma Warrior has a giant drill for a left arm, also. Brawn Hilda: The one female Gamma Warrior is as ugly as her male counterparts. Flat Character: They have no lines, personalities or names; they exist only to give the Hulk something to fight. Hollywood Cyborg: All of the Gamma Warriors have some level of cybernetic components in their bodies. It's unclear if this was to compensate for flaws in the cloning process or an attempt to make them stronger. Mooks: The Gamma Warriors exist to give the Leader some expendable henchmen to throw at the Hulk.

characters.name: Ghost Rider
characters.description: The Ace: Ghost Rider nearly manages to finish off the Hulk, with Hulk only surviving once the Rider was given proof of his innocence. Classical Anti-Hero: Has a rough exterior, but is concerned with protecting innocents. Cold Ham: Has a cooler tone than you'd expect, but no less intense. Dark Is Not Evil: He has a flaming skull andTough Spikes and Studs, but Ghost Rider on the side of good. He only attacked the Hulk out a misunderstanding and realized his error by the end of the episode. Deadly Gaze: The Penance Stare as usual. In his episode, Ghost Rider uses it to kill the Hulk little by little, which could only be thrawted by Rick and Betty coming to Hulk's rescue.
